text:
diego: Heads up — I'm following the browser quickstart (quickstart-web) and I can successfully call GET /models (200) but the streaming websocket connect from the client immediately returns 403. No obvious errors in the server. Using a workspace API key set as REDWOOD_API_KEY in a local .env. Anyone seen REST succeed but streams fail? :thinking:

devex-bot: Ticket created: DEVEX-5412. Please include minimal repro and browser console/network logs.

maya: Which quickstart variant? Is this Vite/react or next? And paste the WS connect request/response from the browser network tab.

diego: vite/react. Browser console snippet:
```
WebSocket connection to 'wss://stream.redwood.ai/v1?model=gpt-small' failed: Error during WebSocket handshake: Unexpected response code: 403
Fetch /v1/models -> 200 OK
WS negotiate POST /v1/auth/negotiate -> 403 Forbidden (response empty)
Client SDK error: websocket auth failed: 403
```
Server logs (dev proxy):
```
INFO: http GET /v1/models 200
WARN: ws auth: workspace key detected from env
ERROR: ws auth: missing X-Redwood-Workspace header -> 403
```

rafael: Interesting. Workspace-scoped service keys require an extra org/workspace header when used from untrusted clients (browser) — that header is usually injected by the server-side SDK or our proxy to prove the request came from a trusted runtime. The quickstart web client should either use a personal API key or run through the local dev proxy that adds X-Redwood-Workspace. If you set a personal key it will work in-browser without that header.

lina: Adding more color: this isn't a billing gate (different from the usual first-call 403). It's an SDK parity/placement issue: the browser SDK's streaming code does not gracefully detect workspace keys and surface an actionable message; it just shows 403. Also the quickstart README doesn't call out that workspace keys are meant for server-side use and will cause WS/stream failures in the browser.

diego: Ok that explains why REST works (we return 200 for model listings) — the listing endpoint tolerates workspace keys from the dev proxy but the WS negotiate requires the workspace header. Workarounds?

maya: Short-term workarounds: 1) Create a personal API key (Profile -> API keys) and set that in your local .env for the browser quickstart. 2) Run the local dev proxy: `npx @redwood/cli proxy` which forwards requests and injects X-Redwood-Workspace for workspace keys. 3) Move the streaming connection to a tiny local server process that uses the workspace key server-side and forwards the stream to the browser.

rafael: Long-term fixes on our side: - Quickstart README update to explicitly warn that workspace/service keys are server-only and will cause WS/stream 403s in browser quickstarts. - SDK change: when the client detects a workspace-scoped key AND receives 403 on WS negotiate, surface an error like: "ERR_WS_WORKSPACE_KEY: Workspace/service keys are server-only. Use a personal key or run the dev proxy: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/quickstarts/web#dev-proxy". - Console UX: mark keys as "Server-only" and show a tooltip if someone tries to copy them into a browser quickstart.

lina: Filed follow-ups in DEVEX-5412: quickstart README change, SDK error code PR, and a small console tweak to label server-only keys. I'll assign the README PR to maya.

diego: Thanks all — `npx @redwood/cli proxy` fixed it immediately. I'll switch to a personal key for the demo and review the quickstart PR. Appreciate the speedy triage :raised_hands:
